$comment: The finding classes the trial has surfaced, one per beads issue. gate.mjs --write classifies a new failing step by the first class whose matchers fit and writes the class's note into trial-baseline.json; a failure no class fits stays unclassified and keeps the gate red. A class is removed here, with its baseline rows, in the PR that fixes the issue.

classes.note: import sql reads FOREIGN KEY targets, not CREATE TABLE statements, and accepts unsupported dialects silently (barwise-1029). The absent names are tables no foreign key points at; on an unsupported dialect the tables that come back are named as the FK clause spells them.
Consequence of barwise-1029: the model import sql produced carries FK-target names ('Cbs.party'), whose DDL export the importer cannot read back. Closes with the parent.

import model --format ddl is a single regex; schema-qualified, bracket-quoted, backtick-quoted and unterminated statements do not match and the only warning claims the file has no CREATE TABLE at all (barwise-1030).
Consequence of barwise-1033 and barwise-1030: the DDL export of the imported model is not readable back by the regex importer. Closes with the parents.
The OpenAPI importer derives role ids from the property name, so two schemas with a 'related' or 'has' property collide and every imported model fails structural/duplicate-role-id (barwise-1031).
Consequence of barwise-1031: the persona's must_validate check fails on the importer's duplicate role ids. Closes with the parent.

Sprint 4 reads each export back through barwise's own importer. The model that comes back carries duplicate role ids and fails validation, which is barwise-1031 reached from the export side: barwise cannot read its own OpenAPI or DDL output into a valid model.

The DDL importer has the same role-id collision as the OpenAPI importer: role ids derived from column names collide across tables and the imported model fails structural/duplicate-role-id (barwise-1031, second importer).
Consequence of barwise-1031 in the DDL importer: the persona's must_validate check fails on duplicate role ids. Closes with the parent.

The default OpenAPI export writes a /* comment */ header when the model has diagnostics (which it always has after barwise-1031), so the .json is not JSON and the importer returns an empty model with exit 0 (barwise-1032).
OpenAPI export then import drops data-type lengths, definitions and value constraints on every value type and loses subtypes beyond the declared loss set (barwise-1042).
DDL export then import is not a fixed point: annotated exports re-import with zero fact types, unannotated ones lose value types and fact types beyond the declared loss set (barwise-1033).
The dbt importer throws 'Fact type X already exists' when two relationship tests derive the same reading, which barwise's own dbt export produces from any ring or double foreign key (barwise-1034).
Reading barwise's own dbt export back throws 'Fact type X already exists' (barwise-1034).
dbt export then import loses value types, definitions, subtypes and objectification beyond the declared loss set (barwise-1035).
NORMA export then import re-homes subset, exclusion and external uniqueness constraints onto sibling fact types and drops definitions, on an importer documented as nearly lossless (barwise-1036).

Reading barwise's own NORMA export back yields a model that fails barwise's own validation with population/mandatory-violation. The cause is the lost `sample: true` flag: NORMA has no seat for a sample instance, so the populations come back significant, their instances enter the object universe, and every mandatory role they must play reports a violation (barwise-1044). Restoring only that flag takes the round-tripped model from 49 errors to 0.
diff reports this rename as a removal plus an addition with no synonym candidate while other renames in the same history are reported as candidates (barwise-1037).
The Kotlin importer returns an empty model for data classes and sealed classes with constructor properties, exit 0, no warning naming a class (barwise-1038).
merge exits 1 with 'Merge produced 1 structural error(s)' on a fact-type rename and does not say which error (barwise-1039).
The release CLI bundle cannot resolve the packaged gym catalog (import.meta.url is empty under cjs) and fails with a Node path error (barwise-1040).

Edit distance to acceptance: the persona's checks fail because the model barwise produced from their artifact is missing the entities the importer dropped (barwise-1029 for sql, barwise-1038 for kotlin, barwise-1031 for openapi). A consequence row; closes with the importer issue it names.
